source.title: Increased decision thresholds enhance information gathering performance in juvenile Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)

confidence_rationale: Two findings pulling opposite ways on MECH-080, in a small sample. It REFUTES the claim's arm-3 assignment (diagnosed OCD showed the extension/over-withholding phenotype the claim reserves for anxiety, not lock-in), while it DEFENDS the claim against its own competence falsifier (OCD patients outperformed controls, so the threshold shift was not degraded competence). n=16 per group caps confidence regardless of how apt the design is.
failure_signatures: Diagnosed OCD patients showed raised decision thresholds and extended sampling -- MECH-080's arm 3 predicts perseverative lock-in for OCD and assigns extended withholding to anxiety, so the observed phenotype is on the wrong arm.

OCD patients scored HIGHER than controls, so the manipulation-of-interest improved rather than degraded performance; any REE result in which shifted commitment timing is accompanied by uniformly worse task performance is therefore NOT reproducing this clinical signature and more likely reflects lost competence.

Sample of 16 per group means a null on any single arm of a three-way dissociation would be uninformative at this power; the claim's dissociation design needs more than this literature currently supports.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Sixteen juvenile OCD patients and sixteen matched controls performed a sequential information-gathering task under manipulated sampling costs. Groups differed in draws-to-decision but not accuracy, and OCD patients achieved significantly more points overall. A Bayesian model with a non-linearly escalating subjective sampling cost attributed the difference to delayed cost emergence and a raised decision threshold in the OCD group.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks directly to MECH-080's own non-degeneracy precondition and falsifier clause. The claim says a failure is uninformative if all effects reduce to lost competence; this paper is a clinical existence proof that a commitment-timing shift can be competence-NEUTRAL or even competence-POSITIVE, which is the pattern a valid REE dissociation would need to reproduce rather than a uniform performance drop.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Diagnosed juvenile OCD is not a REE agent with a deep hippocampal basin, and the paper offers no attractor-dynamics measurement at all -- the inference from 'raised threshold' to 'deep basin' is entirely REE-side and unsupported here. The arm-assignment conflict is the substantive caveat and must be reported, not filed as a detail: this is a diagnosed OCD group presenting with the phenotype MECH-080 assigns to anxiety.
mapping.source_context: Juvenile OCD outpatients vs matched healthy controls, n=16 per group; laboratory sequential sampling task with external cost manipulation; one author declares pharmaceutical speaker honoraria.

confidence_components.notes: Venue and modelling are strong but n=16/16 is small for a case-control group difference and caps source quality at 0.70. Mapping fidelity 0.50: the competence-neutrality finding transfers well, the threshold-to-basin-depth inference does not transfer at all. Transfer risk 0.45 -- juvenile clinical sample, and juvenile OCD may not generalise to adult OCD let alone to a REE rollout parameter.
